name: cipher-docs
description: Cipher usage rules, component guides and the agent skill, for people and coding agents.

files.content:
# v4

This folder is the v4 component source of truth. It is incubating. Product code must not import it. The only UI importer outside this folder is `src/pages/design-system`. Dedicated generation and introspection scripts may read the typed metadata; product code remains fenced from all v4 imports.

For the contribution workflow, read [Infisical UI](skills/infisical-ui/SKILL.md). Its [canonical rules](skills/infisical-ui/rules.json) also drive the workbench Rules page. Every rule, shared or component, has a `detect` field: `lint` names a check in `frontend/scripts/check-v4.ts`, `test` names the test that exercises it, and `review` means only a reader of the change will catch a break. Generation fails on a rule without one.

- Primitives are the shadcn Radix set (`radix-nova`), restyled by `v4.css`. Do not add a second primitive library.
- Colors, type and motion timing (`--v4-duration-*`, `--v4-ease-*`) come from `tokens.json`. Corners are square everywhere: there is no radius scale and no corner mode, so never set a border radius. Do not hard-code hex, raw Tailwind palette classes, or a literal duration or easing.
- The workbench uses a sidebar brand header, a content-width article and responsive comparison cards. Theme and accent sit in the TopBar's workbench menu; there is no floating dock. Brand tokens define its type and color.
- The brand accent is Infisical yellow `--v4-accent` (#e3f047 in both themes), paired with `--v4-on-accent`. The shadcn `bg-accent` role is neutral selection/hover, not the brand accent. Primary (and default, its alias) Buttons are the ink fill for the one main action; only accent Buttons use the shared accent material, for a page's one primary create action (Add new, Create key, New connection) in its header or toolbar, and for approval and grant moments. Save, Confirm, Submit, Download, empty-state actions and every button inside a sheet or dialog stay ink. Keep the global primary role ink and selection neutral: selected and pressed fills step toward a neutral surface in both themes, never a yellow tint. Follow rule/button-material and rule/accent-create in the canonical rules; do not repaint Buttons in examples.
- A fill that is the same in both themes keeps its label color in both themes: on-accent stays near-black on the accent, and the destructive Button is bad-fill with a white on-bad label in both themes. Only fills that flip with theme (ink, the soft status grounds) flip their foreground.
- Use `V4Scope` for the docs boundary and portal container. Workbench theme changes stay local and never update the user's saved theme or analytics.
- Descriptions: every description is optional (PageHeader, Card, Dialog, Sheet, EmptyState, Announcements, ApprovalQueue requests) and used strategically, not removed by reflex. Allowed: a one-sentence page lede, optionally with a Docs link; a one-line dialog or sheet subtitle that scopes the content; short lines that tell cards in a set apart; secondary row lines that carry a state or value. Not allowed: text that restates the title, a lede longer than one sentence, a marketing tagline. A dialog or sheet without a Description is fine: Radix links aria-describedby only while one is mounted (rule/strategic-descriptions).
- Containers: tables are framed (DataTable always; the frameless native Table only inside another surface), lists default to framed and change case by case, and a standalone Card is plain, its default, or no card. Set Card variant framed only for emphasis (org overview product cards, project cards with a footer band) or for a section card that heads part of a page (a detail sidecar, a roles or authentication section, settings sections). Never nest one frame in another (rule/no-nested-frames): Card, DataTable, List, ApprovalQueue and CodeBlock read the frame context from `lib/frame-context.tsx` and provide it to their subtree, so inside a frame a framed Card drops to plain and the others render frameless, embedded on the parent's inset. Overlay portals reset it. A new primitive that draws `frame.frame` must call `useInFrame` and wrap its subtree in `FrameScope`. The `nested-frame` ui:lint check flags an explicit `variant="framed"` inside a framed parent, and a development warning catches the nestings it cannot see (rule/container-defaults). A page CSS module under pages/v4 cannot see the frame it lands in, so it never draws a four-sided border or a non-focus outline around a box: use a frame-aware primitive, the frame's own section or the tint shade, or mark a box that is bordered everywhere with `v4-check-ignore page-css-frame` and the reason (rule/page-boxes-from-primitives, ui:lint page-css-frame).
- Links: Cipher components never import a router. A component that navigates takes `link` and renders `CipherLink` (`lib/link.tsx`); the app types `link` by augmenting `CipherRegister` and wires TanStack once with `V4RouterProvider` (`pages/v4/cipher-router.tsx`) in `V4Root` and the design system. Without the provider, links render plain anchors and Sidebar matches no route. RouteProgress takes `pending` from the app.
- Themes: a theme is a named palette in `tokens.json` `themes.list` (peach, pale, dark; shown as Lightly Peach, Light and Dark) with a `scheme` (light or dark). Every themed token keeps a light and a dark base value; a theme sits on one base (`base`) or extends another theme (`extends`) and lists in `overrides` only what differs, and ui:generate emits one `.v4[data-theme="<id>"]` rule per theme beside the `.v4[data-scheme="dark"]` base. V4Scope sets both `data-theme` (the theme id) and `data-scheme` on its root and portals. Branch on the scheme, never the theme name: `[data-scheme="dark"]` in CSS and `useV4Scheme()` in code (logos, charts, toasts); `useV4Theme()` is only for passing the theme on, such as a `?theme=` preview. Legacy `light` maps to peach and the retired `dark-alt` to dark everywhere a theme is read (V4Scope props, ancestors, stored preferences, `?theme=`). To add a theme, add its entry with only its overrides and run ui:generate; the pickers, the Color page and `docs/themes.md` (contrast per theme) pick it up. The live app keeps light, dark or system in the shared theme preference and remembers the named theme per scheme in localStorage `v4-theme`, so System resolves to the person's chosen light and dark themes (rule/theme-scheme, ui:lint theme-name-branch).
- `V4Scope` portals into `document.body` by default. Pass `portalContainer` to place its overlays inside a frame instead; that element must establish a containing block (transform or `contain: layout`) so fixed overlays stay within it. Popper-based contents pass `useV4CollisionBoundary()` as `collisionBoundary` so they flip and shift inside that frame; it is undefined for body portals.
- Every overlay content, submenus included, portals into that container at the one overlay layer (z-50); a nested overlay mounts after its parent and paints above it by DOM order. Never render overlay content inline inside another overlay or raise one overlay's z-index. Toasts portal into the V4Scope toast layer, a sibling placed right after that container, so they paint above every sheet and dialog on the same z-50 layer. AppShell mounts the one Toaster; Toaster renders once per toaster id, so a page that still mounts its own never duplicates a toast.
- Orgs have no avatar. Composites and compositions don't use avatars until the product supports them: show names and emails as plain text. The Avatar primitive and its docs page stay.
- After UI edits, run `npm run lint` in `frontend/`. Also run `npm run lint:v4` and `npm run ui:lint`. `ui:lint` runs the v4 checks against a baseline that only shrinks: a new finding fails, a fixed one is locked in with `npm run ui:lint -- --update`. Exempt one line with `v4-check-ignore <check> -- <reason>` on it or the line above; the reason is required. `lint:v4` is `@shadcn/lint` (`no-raw-colors`, `no-restyle`) as an Oxlint JS plugin on the docs route, configured in `.oxlintrc.v4.json` and kept out of `npm run lint`. The import fence and the relaxations for `v4/ui` and `v4/hooks` live in `.oxlintrc.json`. Do not add spacing or type classes to a v4 component. Wrap it instead.
- Add components with `npx shadcn@4.22.0 add <name> -y` from `frontend/`, which reads `components.json`. Do not run `shadcn init` here. It would retarget the app. The CLI resolves aliases from the root `tsconfig.json`, which is a solution file and must not gain a `paths` block: that slows the frontend lint past its 15 minute CI cap. If add cannot resolve `@app/*`, copy the `paths` block from `tsconfig.app.json` for that command only, and do not commit it.
- Primitives import `cn` from the `cn` package. That is the registry's helper. Do not rewrite those imports.
- These unrelated upstream items remain outside this React 19 foundation: attachment, bubble, direction, marker, message, message-scroller, questionnaire, trace.

Read the generated component guides in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) or run `npm run ui:info -- <name>` from frontend. `npm run ui:generate` refreshes tokens, the catalog, documentation and standard registry payloads; `npm run ui:check` detects stale output and missing contracts. Start `npm run dev` and open `/design-system` in the app. Verification recipes in metadata are not passing evidence.

The registry is published publicly as Cipher (`@cipher/<item>`, base item `cipher-base`); see [cipher/README.md](../../../../cipher/README.md). `npm run cipher:release` regenerates it and copies the payloads to `cipher/r/`, which consumers fetch from raw GitHub URLs, so run it only for a release. Every registry file must work outside this app: an item that needs Infisical data, routes or app assets goes in `excludedFromRegistry` in `scripts/generate-ui.ts` with its reason, and generation fails when a published item depends on an excluded one.

## Human examples

Use the shared preview frame and ExampleGrid, ExampleCell and ExampleStage presentation components. Compare supported variants, distinct sizes and applicable states as labeled peers. Captions sit 8px below their own specimen and describe its actual state. Specimens and captions align to the start, and specimens in a row share a bottom baseline, so the captions of a row line up. Equal-appearance aliases share one specimen. Keep specimens in one row of similar height; give a much taller one its own row.

Use only the composition needed to demonstrate the component. Do not add synthetic save/reject/reset controls, request logs, export workflows or stress-test toolbars to Human pages. Ordinary action buttons do not become pressed toggles merely to produce feedback. Keep core interactions working and relevant states visible. Put technical orchestration in component tests and explain constraints in the closed Usage and rules disclosure. Generated Agent examples lower documentation-only presentation wrappers to native layout elements, so they remain portable.

## Icons

The v4 line set (52 glyphs from #8691, ui/icon-data.ts) is the primary icon set: use `<Icon name="..." />`. Use Lucide (`lucide-react`) only for glyphs the set lacks (Kbd keys, the unsorted sort arrows and similar), through `<Icon icon={...} />` or a direct import, drawn at `stroke-icon` (1.7) and the size tokens so it blends in. Do not hand-draw other SVG icons or import another icon library.

## System rules

- Disable, do not hide: a blocked action stays visible and disabled, with a reason, so the layout never shifts. A Button takes the reason as disabledReason, which keeps it focusable and shows the reason in a tooltip. Never wrap a natively disabled Button in a Tooltip or a span anchor: it takes no pointer or focus events, so the reason never reaches keyboard users (rule/disabled-reason-tooltip, ui:lint disabled-in-tooltip). Tooltips are pass-through: TooltipContent has pointer-events none and user-select none and the provider disables hoverable content, and TooltipTrigger opens on keyboard navigation focus only, so focus a menu, dialog or sheet returns never reopens it, and stays closed after a click until the pointer leaves and returns. Hovered, selectable or copyable content uses HoverCard, and actions use Popover (rule/tooltip-pass-through, ui:lint `interactive-tooltip`). Table wraps its rows in TooltipScope, so every Tooltip in a Table or DataTable shares one Radix root that mounts on first use; keep row tooltips uncontrolled (no open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange or delayDuration), or each one falls back to its own root. Gate each action by its own permission only; a person who may view a secret may copy it while it is masked.
- Pickers for entities a person may need to create first (app connections, gateways) pass Combobox `creation` with mode dialog, gated by disabledReason on the create permission. The Combobox owns the Dialog, its Cancel and submit, and routes every close through useDiscardChangesGuard. For app connections use `connectionCreation` with a preset from `pages/v4/data/integrations/connection-presets.ts`; presets take their schemas from `lib/schemas/app-connections.ts`, the same ones the v3 forms use. A redirect method (GitHub App install, OAuth) needs `redirect: connectionRedirect({ returnTo, projectId, option })` (`pages/v4/data/integrations/connection-redirect.ts`) from the caller, where `returnTo` is the calling flow's v4 href: it stores the state and half-filled form under `V4_CONNECTION_REDIRECT_STORAGE_KEY` (`helpers/appConnections.ts`, which main's `OAuthCallbackPage` reads to forward a matching state to v4) and the v4 callback route (`pages/v4/organization/AppConnectionCallbackPage`) creates the connection and returns there with `connectionId` and `connectionName`, so read those search params instead of adding a per-flow callback.
- Row actions are persistent: they live in the table's actions tail, the sticky last column (DataTable `rowActions`, or `TableActionsCell` with `RowActions` in a native Table) and show on every row at rest. Use at most three inline icon actions, then the More menu for the rest. Nothing a hover or focus shows may change a cell's width or the row's layout, so there is no hover reveal and no indicator that swaps out for actions; this overrides matching main's hover actions. The actions tail end-aligns its actions, so the last one sits at the inset on every row, and takes its width from the widest row: size-row (a square) for one, plus size-row-action-step for each further action. Every actions tail (rowActions, TableActionsCell, a column with actions true) caps its Buttons at size-target-row, so a text button like Open is 28px tall like icon-row; never set a width, size or padding on an actions tail. Row stripe, selection and hover are layers the pinned cells repaint opaquely, so a row reads as one band to the frame edge. The DataTable selection column is size-row wide with a persistent line-soft divider on its right.
- One hover color: every neutral hover ground (sidebar rows and tools, table, list, tree and grid rows, menu rows, segments, ghost and outline actions, tiles) is `var(--v4-hover)`, and pressed is `var(--v4-press)`. Both are translucent `mix-ink` (ink, or peach's warm dark neutral), so they land on whatever ground is underneath, darken it in light schemes and brighten it in dark ones, with no per-theme value; tune the strength in one place with `hover-mix` and `press-mix`. Where a fill must be opaque (a pinned cell, a ring that cuts out a dot), mix `var(--v4-mix-ink)` at `var(--v4-hover-mix)` into that ground with `color-mix(in srgb, ...)`, which matches how the overlay composites. `sidebar-current` is `mix-ink` at `current-mix` mixed into the sidebar, a small step past hover, and `selected-surface` takes its alpha from `selected-mix`. The sidebar's hover highlight is `var(--v4-sidebar-hover)`, which follows `sidebar-current` unless a theme quiets it. Never give a hovered element a flat ground such as tint or surface (rule/translucent-hover, ui:lint `flat-hover`).
- Cursor: styled controls keep the default cursor, even when they render an anchor: Button in every variant but link, toggles, Select, Combobox and MultiSelect triggers, menu, Switcher, Sidebar and nav sheet rows, Tabs, crumb switcher triggers, row actions, Checkbox, Radio and Switch. Only links take cursor: pointer: text anchors, RowLink and CardLink, crumb names that navigate, the link Button and unstyled text buttons that read as links (rule/pointer-cursor-for-links, ui:lint cursor-pointer). The check passes a CSS selector that names a link (a, [href], :any-link, or link in a class or attribute name) and flags every Tailwind cursor-pointer and inline pointer cursor. Anything else that reads as a link marks its rule with v4-check-ignore cursor-pointer and the reason; in CSS the marker may sit in a comment right before the rule.
- Line roles: line-soft is the default border, the outward edge of every inset surface, card, plain list, table, popover, dialog and bordered tile, the app shell chrome (AppInset island, band rule, sidebar edge and separators) and every divider that touches one of those edges. line is only for a standalone rule that touches no other border: a section rule, the band's divider marks, a lone hr, a tree guide, the tab track, chart axes. Control borders keep their control tokens (rule/line-roles, ui:lint line-on-edge flags a four-sided line border).
- No left accent bars: never mark a row, card, Alert or current state with a colored stripe or tinted left edge, even where main does. Use a translucent tint over the whole row or surface plus a Badge or icon with text. Tree guides, timeline connectors and dividers in line or line-soft are structure, not accents.
- Loading: while a whole page or its lazy chunk loads, show the page loader (Loader size page) as the Suspense fallback or page body. Inside a rendered page, show Skeleton shapes when the loaded shape is known, the table's loading rows for rows in a table on screen, and Loader only when the shape is unknown.
- Placeholders and values: every field placeholder, in Input, Textarea, SecretInput, the SensitiveEditor replacement box and any textarea or contenteditable value editor (a `::before` or `data-placeholder` placeholder included), is `var(--v4-muted)`, the color of the shared `.field ::placeholder` rule in controls.module.css, so placeholders read the same everywhere. Never dim one to faint, which is for disabled text, or repaint one in a page stylesheet. Secret values, typed or masked, and their placeholders use the body role in the UI sans; keep Geist Mono for read-only literal machine text such as code blocks, IDs and keys.
- Row focus: while a row is being edited in place (its annotation popover, an inline name or value edit), set `focused` on its TableRow or pass DataTable `focusedRowId`, and clear it when the edit closes; the other rows of that body, and of every body that holds it, dim to `opacity-row-dim`. Never use it for selection or a current record, and never dim rows with a page's own opacity or filter (rule table-row-focus).
- No :has(): never write a :has() selector or a Tailwind has-* variant in v4 CSS or classes; Chrome re-checks it on DOM changes far from the element, so one cell update in a large table relayouts the page. Set a data attribute from props, a child's context report (lib/presence-count.ts) or useDescendantFlags (lib/descendant-flags.ts) and select on that (rule/no-has-selectors, ui:lint has-selector).
- Focus: fields, slider thumbs and other glow-focused controls share one glow, size-focus-glow in focus-ring (neutral ink, never the accent).
- Menus: every menu-like popover (Switcher, account menu, DropdownMenu, Select and Combobox lists, ContextMenu, CommandMenu) uses the shared recipe in menu.module.css: pop ground, pop-line edge and shadow-pop, a 3px inset on all four sides, 32px rows as inset blocks, eyebrow labels and one lead-icon column. Separators may span the panel; rows and their tints never touch its edge.
- Shared highlight: every vertical selectable list (menus, Select, MultiSelect, Combobox, CommandMenu, Switchers, the Sidebar nav) draws two translucent thumbs from `ListHighlight` in lib/list-highlight.tsx, rendered as the list's last child. The hover thumb follows the pointer and the keyboard's active row and stays on the last row while the pointer is anywhere in the panel, gaps, labels and separators included; it hides when the pointer leaves the panel, the menu closes or keyboard focus leaves. The selection thumb rests on the current row and shows only while the hover thumb is hidden, cross-fading on fade.enter. Keyboard entry starts the hover thumb on the current row. Thumbs measure offsets inside the list (never viewport rects), stay hidden until their first measurement, appear in place without gliding from a stale spot, and glide on spring.moderate after that; reduced motion jumps. Rows in such a list draw no tint of their own, and the current row keeps its 600 weight and check. An expanded row (aria-haspopup with aria-expanded true or data-state open: a rail flyout, a submenu parent, a Switcher row opening a nested list) pins the hover thumb until its popover closes, even with the pointer inside the popover; ListHighlight derives this from the trigger, so call sites add nothing.
- Triggers defer to Button: a menu, popover or select trigger takes Button's rest, hover, pressed, open and focus states on the whole control. Never draw an inner tint inside a bordered control.
- Fonts: Archivo is the sans for everything people read and name; Geist Mono is only for machine values a person copies or compares character by character (secret keys, IDs, hashes, fingerprints, serials, hosts, paths, env var names, code, key IDs, optionally aligned numbers). Names people chose (project, organization, environment, role, group, identity, user, folder, key, certificate common name, connection) stay in the sans, in crumbs, switchers, titles and table primaries too. A slug takes mono only where it is shown or edited as the slug. Never set a font family on html, body, V4Scope, AppShell or a theme, and reach mono only through a primitive's mono prop or the mono type role on a machine value. DataTable primary is sans; a column opts in with mono (rule/mono-machine-values, ui:lint mono-named-entity).
- Triggers start-align their value: Select, Combobox, MultiSelect and any Button that opens a menu, popover or picker put the label at the start, truncate it and put the chevron at the end. A Button trigger passes `layout="trigger"`, which draws the chevron and takes SelectTrigger's insets; never center the value or add `iconRight="chev-down"` to a plain Button (rule/trigger-start-aligned, ui:lint trigger-start-aligned).
- Tab width: Tabs and ToggleGroup take one width prop that sizes the track and its triggers together. The default, content, fits the track to its triggers; full stretches the track and gives every trigger an equal share. Never set a width, flex or grow on a tab list, track or trigger, so a full-width track never holds content-width triggers (rule/tab-width, ui:lint tab-width). The underline variant's rule is a divider and spans its container under content-width triggers; UNDERLINE_RULE_SPANS in ui/tabs.tsx is the one switch for it.
- Chevron tiles: a trailing chevron sits at the far edge only on an item with its own ground. Use Tile, which is bordered on a bare surface and takes the tint shade instead inside a framed Card, List or DataTable; on an unframed item the chevron follows its content (rule/chevron-tile-frame).
- Kbd: caps are size-kbd-md (20px), size-kbd-sm (18px) or size-kbd-xs (16px, tooltips). Single glyphs are square; longer labels grow with equal side padding. A host slot sets --v4-kbd-host-block and --v4-kbd-host-end so the trailing gap equals the vertical gap.
- What's new: the Overview's "What's new" list (`recentChanges` in `pages/design-system/overview-data.ts`) is kept by hand. Every push with a user-visible system change adds one entry, newest first: `id`, `title`, a one-sentence `description` in v4 voice, `date`, the short `commit`, and `page` (a `workbenchPages` id) when a workbench page shows it. Merge closely related changes into one entry so it reads as a changelog, keep about 15 entries, and drop the oldest past that.

## Workbench comparisons

`/design-system` has a Comparisons group: one page per product screen with a before/after slider (`pages/design-system/comparison-slider.tsx`). Before is a committed WebP of the current app on main (`assets/comparisons/<screen>-<light|dark>.webp`, 1706x971 at 2x, seeded data). After is an iframe of the screen's routed demo page in the v4 app (`/v4/organizations/demo/...`, see `pages/v4`), laid out at 1706x971, scaled to the stage, and given the workbench theme through `?theme=`. Each comparison's `href` lives in `pages/design-system/navigation.ts`, and the Access captures map to theirs in `access-views.ts`. The handle drags, takes Left and Right (Shift for 10%), Home and End, and Reset returns it to the page's start. "Live, full width" links to the routed page itself.

## Workbench navigation and search

The workbench itself runs in a real AppShell on real routes: `/design-system` is the Overview, and every other page is `/design-system/foundations/$page`, `/design-system/components/$group/$component`, `/design-system/patterns/$pattern` or `/design-system/comparisons/$comparison` (virtual routes in `src/routes.ts`, files in `pages/design-system/routes/`). `navigation.ts` is the route manifest: each page carries its typed `link`, and the Sidebar levels, the TopBar crumbs and switchers, and the palette all read it. Route definitions load with main's entry, so they import nothing from the design system or v4 (the bundle fence fails the build otherwise): validation and redirects live in the split components. The layout sends old `#<page>` URLs on `/design-system` to their route (`legacyHashLink`), a page route with an unknown slug and `/design-system/$` (category paths, unknown pages) navigate to the first page they name, and `pendingComponent` is a `lazyRouteComponent`. The TopBar band's breadcrumb reads category, group (components only) and page, its account menu is the Workbench menu (pages, links, theme and accent), the v4 Sidebar takes `levels` (a top level with Overview and the four categories, then one level per category, Components with one eyebrow section per group, each with an icon so the rail shows one flyout row per group), and AppInset. Mod+B toggles the sidebar (AppShell owns the chord, so it works the same in every shell). Mod+K and the TopBar search button open the command palette (`pages/design-system/workbench-palette.tsx`, built on CommandMenu). Its index is derived from `navigation.ts` and the generated catalog, so every page, alias and example section is searchable without a hand-kept list. An example result navigates to its page with the example id as the hash, and the page scrol... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
- Page content width: the size-content token (1160px) sets the page gutter that AppInset derives and PageGutter pads by. Wrap page content in PageGutter; never cap it with mx-auto and an arbitrary max-w.
- Detail pages that pair one details card with stacked content cards use DetailLayout: the sidecar (size-sidecar) sits on the right and stacks above the content below size-sidecar-collapse of the layout's own width. Never hand-build that two-column grid. Record facts in those cards use DataList density compact, with short values paired by span half.
- Status cells: report a state with StatusText (a line icon plus words), never color alone or a brand mark, and derive it only from fields the API returns.
- Bulk selection uses the floating action bar (FloatingActionBar), never an inline bar. Selecting or clearing rows must not move layout. The bar is fixed to the bottom center of the window on every page, even where it crosses the sidebar; it portals into the V4Scope overlay container at z-index 40, above page content and sticky headers and below every z-50 overlay and toast. While it shows it pads AppInset by its height plus its offset, so the last rows and the pagination scroll clear of it. Pass it to DataTable's actionBar when a DataTable holds the selection and never position it yourself (rule/selection-floating-action-bar).
- Tables and list pages follow one recipe:
  - A row that goes to the record's page puts RowLink in its primary cell; never navigate from onRowActivate (rule/row-navigation-link, ui:lint row-activate-navigates).
  - A row that opens its record in a Sheet or Dialog uses onRowActivate plus a quiet link Button (variant link, underline hover: underlined only on hover and keyboard focus) with the record's name in the primary cell. It has no RowLink, so no chevron, and no Open action in the tail; a URL-addressable sheet may use RowLink with chevron={false} (rule/sheet-row-open).
  - Pagination goes in DataTable's pagination slot with variant="compact", never as a sibling after the table (rule/pagination-in-frame, ui:lint pagination-outside-frame).
  - Action results (copied, saved, deleted, moved, uploaded, failed) are toasts, never footer or status-line text; DataTable's persistentStatus holds only state that must stay visible, such as "Showing 5 of 120 after filter" (rule/toast-action-feedback, ui:lint action-feedback-in-status).
  - A hand-built Table row with RowActions or a TableActionsCell wraps itself in RowContextMenu (rule/row-context-menu, ui:lint row-actions-without-context-menu).
  - Resource lists inline the one most-used non-destructive action, such as Edit, Rotate or View logs, then More; destructive actions stay in More (rule/row-actions-inline-primary).
  - Full list pages search and filter with FilterBar, which drops Add filter when it has no fields; a search box with an icon-only filter menu is only for search inside a Card header (rule/list-page-filter-bar).
  - A table inside a Card or SettingsCard is a DataTable; the native Table is for the secrets matrix and dialog, sheet and popover internals (rule/detail-card-data-table, ui:lint raw-table-in-card).
  - A detail page's facts card uses DataList density compact (rule/detail-facts-compact).
  - pages/v4 findings for these checks sit in scripts/check-v4-baseline.json until the sweep fixes them.
- v4 paths: never write the /v4 prefix as a literal in pages/v4 or components/v4 (to=, href=, navigate, redirect, startsWith, regular expressions). Build links through the v4 link helpers in pages/v4/links.ts (orgHref, useGo); the resolver is src/helpers/v4Bridge.ts. Moving v4 to the root at launch is then a change to those modules and the route definitions only. Route definition files and the modules in the check's v4PathModules list (scripts/check-v4.ts) may spell it, and a route ID passed as a from: value or to getRouteApi is exempt because TanStack type-checks it; anything else that must takes v4-check-ignore v4-path-literal with a reason (rule/v4-path-helper, ui:lint v4-path-literal).

# Component guide

# Access list Who can reach a project: a member per row that opens them, multiple selection with the bulk bar and a locked owner. ## Choose this component Choose AccessList for a membership list with bulk changes. Use a Table when people need to sort, filter or export members. ## Usage rules ### access-list-roles Owner: access-list. When a member has a role or temporary access. Do: Name the role in a Badge and say when temporary access ends, such as Read, 1 hour. Avoid: Color-code roles or hide the expiry in a tooltip. Why: Words survive both themes and screen readers; color alone does not. Checked by: review only. Look for: Read each row's badge and description for the role and any expiry. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/patterns/access-list.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/access-list/default.tsx ### access-list-owner Owner: access-list. When a member cannot lose access, such as the owner. Do: Make the row unselectable, disable its menu and say why in the description. Avoid: Let the owner be selected and fail the bulk action. Why: A control that cannot succeed should not be offered. Checked by: review only. Look for: Select all and check the owner stays unselected. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/patterns/access-list.tsx ## State guidance - revoked: Rows leave the list and a toast offers Undo for the undo window. - empty: A small empty state with a bare icon says nobody else has access yet. ## Presentation rules Do: Say how each member got access in plain words. Avoid: Show internal policy identifiers as the description. Why: People decide on access by who granted it and why. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/patterns/access-list.tsx - src/components/v4/patterns/patterns.module.css Exports: AccessList. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - A toolbar above the list says how many have access and offers Add member. - Members are link rows in a framed List with selection, the member's name as text, the role as a Badge, how they got access, last use and a row menu. - Selecting rows raises the FloatingActionBar with Revoke access. The owner cannot be selected and its menu is disabled. - After a revoke, a success toast says how many lost access and offers Undo for 10 seconds, the undo window; Undo calls onRestore and toasts the result. The revoke is already committed through onRevoke, so the window ending only closes the toast. A failed revoke or restore is an error toast that stays until dismissed, and the rows stay. ## Accessibility - The List's select-all and row checkboxes are named for the member; the bulk bar is a named toolbar with a count status. - The toast region announces each revoke, restore and failure, so the pattern has no status line of its own. When the revoked rows leave the list and focus went with them, focus moves to the next remaining member's name, or the previous one at the end, or the list itself when nobody is left. - Machine and agent names are names people chose, so they stay in the sans like a person's name; the kind shows in the media and badge (rule/mono-machine-values). ## Use cases - Use AccessList for who can reach one project or resource, with roles in words and temporary access saying when it ends. ## Avoid - Color roles, or confirm every revoke with a dialog when Undo can restore it. ## Limits - The host owns the members and persists revokes and restores. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. # Combobox Search and choose one option from a provided list. ## Choose this component Choose Combobox when a known option list needs search. Use TagsInput when people type the values and there is no list to pick from, SecretPathInput for a folder path typed segment by segment, Select for a short grouped choice and CommandMenu for executing actions. ## Usage rules ### combobox-usage Owner: combobox. When several options share similar display labels. Do: Give each option a stable unique value and useful searchable text; keep the selected label visible when filtering. Avoid: Use array indexes as identity or commit the first result just because the query changed. Why: Filtering narrows candidates without choosing a value. Checked by: review only. Look for: Filter similar options, highlight one and cancel. Query/highlight do not change the committed value until selection, and distinct stable option ids survive reordered results. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/combobox.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/combobox/default.tsx ### combobox-dialog-creation Owner: combobox. When people may need to create the entity they are picking first, such as an app connection or a gateway. Do: Pass creation with mode dialog and a renderForm that reports dirty and pending and calls complete with the created option, and set disabledReason when the person may not create one. Avoid: Send people to another page to create the entity, hide the Create row without the permission, or close the Dialog from the form without the discard guard. Why: Creating in place keeps the flow and its draft, and routing every close through one guard means a dirty form is never lost by accident. Checked by: src/components/v4/ui/combobox.test.tsx. Opens the dialog row, edits the form and cancels: the discard prompt opens and Keep editing keeps the Dialog. Submitting calls complete, which selects the new option on the trigger and closes the Dialog. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/combobox.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/app-connection-form/default.tsx ### combobox-searchable-value Owner: combobox. When a field searches an in-memory set or offers host-backed creation. Do: Use stable option values, keep the visible field purpose separate from the query and pass onCreate only for a real cancellable host operation. Avoid: Treat an empty search as an empty collection, create duplicate values, imply in-memory search is remote or filter again on top of onSearch results. Why: Query state, selected identity and persisted creation describe different things and must not be conflated. Checked by: review only. Look for: Search without matches, reject creation and retry, then close during a pending request. Selected identity stays correct and obsolete results do not select themselves. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/combobox.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/combobox/default.tsx ### combobox-free-text-tags Owner: combobox. When people type a list of values that no option list holds, such as domains, redirect URIs or claim values. Do: Use TagsInput, with validate for format rules and onValidationChange feeding the Field error. Avoid: Fake it with Combobox multiple whose options mirror the value and whose onCreate appends the query. Why: A tag list has no options to search, so a picker adds an empty list, a Create row and a second source of truth for the value. Checked by: review only. Look for: Type a value and press Enter, type a comma, paste a comma and newline separated list with one invalid entry and press Backspace in the empty input. # Context Menu Expose secondary actions from a context menu. ## Choose this component Choose ContextMenu for shortcuts on an already discoverable object. Use DropdownMenu when the action entry point must be visible. ## Usage rules ### context-menu-usage Owner: context-menu. When an essential action appears in a right-click menu. Do: Provide the same action through a visible button or menu, and make the context trigger keyboard reachable. Avoid: Make right-click the only way to inspect, copy or restore an object. Why: Touch users and people who do not discover context menus still need the action. Checked by: review only. Look for: Complete the essential object action without right-clicking; the visible alternative and Shift+F10 context route both reach the intended action. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/context-menu.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/context-menu/default.tsx ## State guidance - disabled: Explain why a locked action is unavailable in surrounding object detail. - copy: Announce copied only after the clipboard write fulfills; show a failure if it rejects. ## Presentation rules Do: Name menu actions for the object under the pointer. Avoid: Fill the menu with disabled coming-soon entries. Why: Unavailable placeholders hide the actions a person can use now. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/context-menu.tsx Exports: ContextMenu, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuPortal, ContextMenuRadioGroup, ContextMenuRadioItem, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut, ContextMenuSub, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuTrigger. # Dropdown Menu Choose an action or setting from a trigger menu. ## Choose this component Choose DropdownMenu for a short set of actions or checked preferences behind a visible trigger. Use Popover for editable controls and Select for a form value. ## Usage rules ### dropdown-menu-usage Owner: dropdown-menu. When a menu includes a dangerous operation among ordinary actions. Do: Separate the destructive item, name its consequence, and let the host confirm when necessary. Avoid: Put a multi-field form or an unguarded irreversible action in a generic More menu. Why: Menu selection closes quickly and is unsuitable for a draft that needs validation. Checked by: review only. Look for: Use the menu with keyboard only. Action items do what their labels name, checked items reflect owner state and editable tasks use a suitable form surface. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/dropdown-menu/default.tsx ### dropdown-menu-nested-layers Owner: dropdown-menu. When an overlay opens from inside another one: a submenu, a popover, select or dialog launched from a menu, or a tooltip inside a popover. Do: Let every overlay portal into the V4Scope container at the one overlay layer (z-50). The child opens after its parent, so it mounts later in that container and paints above it. Avoid: Render overlay content inline inside another overlay, or give one overlay a higher z-index or an isolating className to win a stacking fight. Why: Inline content is clipped by its parent's overflow and placed in its parent's transformed frame, so a submenu that flips can land behind the panel it came from. Checked by: src/components/v4/ui/overlay-regressions.test.tsx. Opens a submenu from an open DropdownMenu and checks the submenu sits outside the parent panel, in the same scope container, after it in DOM order. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx ## State guidance - checked: Control checkbox and radio items from actual preference state. - pending: Keep continuing operation feedback outside the menu after it closes. ## Presentation rules Do: Keep the trigger label tied to the object or action set. Avoid: Use several adjacent unlabeled ellipsis buttons for different action sets. Why: Identical hidden menus make the correct action hard to locate. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/menu-content.tsx Exports: DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuPortal, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubContent, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuTrigger. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Highlighted, open and active rows use a translucent ink overlay at the shared hover token, so the menu surface behind shows through; they never take an opaque fill. - Open menus retain Radix typeahead and directional keys. Shortcut text requires a matching host handler. - Radix Root owns open/onOpenChange. Action items close after onSelect; checkbox/radio changes stay open by default and can opt into closeOnSelect. - DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem and DropdownMenuRadioItem take an optional description, a muted second line under the label. # Duration input Enter a length of time as an amount and a unit, in the ms() string main sends. ## Choose this component Choose DurationInput when the API takes an ms() duration string. Use a number Input with its own unit Select only when the API stores seconds or another number, and Calendar or a date field for a point in time. ## Usage rules ### duration-input-ms-string Owner: duration-input. When a form sends a duration such as temporaryRange or maxTimePeriod to an API that parses it with ms(). Do: Bind value and onChange to the one string field, validate it with ms() in the host, and pass invalid with the Field error. Avoid: Rebuild the string from a separate amount and unit, or accept free text that ms() reads differently from what the person meant. Why: The string is the API contract main already sends; a second format drifts from it and free text hides typos until the request fails. Checked by: review only. Look for: Type an amount and change the unit, then read the bound value: it is the amount followed by one of s, m, h, d or w, and an empty amount gives an empty string. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/duration-input.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/duration-input/default.tsx ## State guidance - empty: Keep the unit on Hours or the last choice so the next keystroke forms a full value. - invalid: Say what to change in the Field error, such as Enter a duration greater than 0. ## Presentation rules Do: Show the policy limit in the Field description or error, in the policy's own words. Avoid: Clamp the amount silently or swap the unit behind the person's back. Why: A silent change grants a different duration from the one the person asked for. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/duration-input.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/duration-input.module.css Exports: DurationInput, DurationInputProps, DurationUnit. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Controlled: value and onChange(value: string) carry the same string main's v3 DurationInput sends for access request durations and policy time periods: the amount followed by s, m, h, d or w, such as 1h, 30m, 7d or 1.5h. Clearing the amount emits an empty string. Pass the value to the API as it is. - The amount is a native number Input (decimal input mode, min 0.001, any step) and the unit is a Select of Seconds, Minutes, Hours, Days and Weeks, side by side at the 32px control height. A new field starts on Hours. Changing the unit with an amount emits the new string at once; with no amount it only sets the unit for the next keystroke. - A value it cannot split, such as 1 hour, shows an empty amount. A bare number is read as milliseconds and shown in the largest whole unit, like main, for values saved before units were required. - invalid draws the invalid border on both controls, and so does the error of a surrounding Field. disabled disables both. ## Accessibility - Label it with Field or aria-label. # Field mapping Map each source field to the value or name it becomes, one aligned row per field. ## Choose this component Choose FieldMapping for two or more fixed source fields that each need a value. Use a single Field for one input, and DataList to show a mapping that cannot be edited. ## Usage rules ### field-mapping-control-height Owner: field-mapping. When a source label sits in the same row as the Input it maps to. Do: Let FieldMappingRow render the source as a control-height Badge that matches the Input size. Avoid: A compact 20px Badge or a hand-sized span beside a 32px Input. Why: A badge that shares a row with regular-height controls takes the control height, so the row reads as one band and the arrow centers on both. Checked by: review only. Look for: Measure a mapping row: the source Badge, the arrow cell and the Input share one height. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/patterns/field-mapping.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/field-mapping/default.tsx ### field-mapping-sentence-case Owner: field-mapping. When writing the header row. Do: Name both columns in sentence case for what they hold, such as Source field and Secret name. Avoid: Title Case headers like Rotated Credentials, or an empty header over the inputs. Why: The headers are the only visible labels for the inputs. Checked by: review only. Look for: Read the header row for sentence case and a noun per column. Source evidence: - src/pages/design-system/examples/field-mapping/default.tsx ## State guidance - invalid: The FieldError sits under its own Input; the source Badge and arrow stay put. ## Presentation rules Do: Use a soft Badge with the field's own glyph for the source. Avoid: Color each source by status or add a left accent bar to the row. Why: The source is a name, not a state. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/patterns/field-mapping.tsx - src/components/v4/patterns/field-mapping.module.css Exports: FieldMapping, FieldMappingRow. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - FieldMapping is a fieldset with a visually hidden legend and a three-column grid: a sentence case header row (sourceHeader, then targetHeader with an optional targetHint such as an InfoTip), then one FieldMappingRow per field. The grid keeps every source, arrow and input in one column track, so the columns align however long a source name is. - Each FieldMappingRow is a soft source Badge at the row's control height (size control-sm, control-md or control-lg, from FieldMapping size), a muted arrow glyph centered on the same height, and an Input of the matching size. The Badge stretches to the source column with its label at the start, so every arrow lines up. - FieldMappingRow takes every Input prop except size and invalid, so trailing, mono, placeholder, value, onChange and ref pass straight through. A trailing slot keeps the Input's nested slot: put the compact Badge (default md) there, not a control-height one. error renders a FieldError under the Input and marks it invalid. - The Input's accessible name defaults to targetHeader for source (Secret name for Access key ID); pass aria-label to replace it. ## Accessibility - The legend names the whole group. Each Input is named by its source and the target header, so a screen reader hears which field it maps without seeing the grid. The arrow is decorative and hidden. ## Use cases - Use FieldMapping wherever a form maps named source fields to secret names or values: rotation credentials, honey token keys, sync and import mappings. ## Avoid - Build a page-local grid of a span chip, an arrow and an Input. FieldMapping replaces those layouts. ## Limits - The target column is always an Input. A mapping whose target is a Select, or whose direction runs from a picked column to a fixed field, is not covered yet. - The host owns values, validation and defaults; FieldMapping only lays the rows out. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. # Field Connect a control to its label, description and validation error. ## Choose this component Choose Field to connect a control with its label, help and error. Use FieldSet and FieldLegend for a group rather than assigning one label to several controls. ## Usage rules ### field-usage Owner: field. When a control fails validation after submission. Do: Keep the entered value, associate the field-specific error with the focusable control and explain the repair without repeating the label. Avoid: Put an error beside an unlabeled wrapper or show unrelated help and error as competing instructions. Why: The person needs one clear repair instruction attached to the value they can change, not repeated helper copy competing with the error. Checked by: review only. Look for: Activate each visible label and inspect the focused control's accessible description. Its own help/error is associated, and entered values survive invalid submission. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/field.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/field/default.tsx ### field-association-and-validation Owner: field. When a form control has a label, help and validation error. Do: Use Field for supported automatic association, or connect explicit ids and ARIA descriptions for custom and compound controls; keep the label visible. Avoid: Assume every child consumes Field context, use placeholder text as the label or show an invalid color with no associated explanation. Why: Visual proximity does not create an accessible label or tell the person how to correct the value. Checked by: review only. Look for: Focus each control with an error and inspect its name and description associations. The visible error is reachable, and custom controls retain explicit wiring. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/field.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/field/default.tsx ## State guidance - optional: Mark optionality in the label area without replacing the control name. - invalid: Retain the entered value and use an actionable field-specific error. ## Presentation rules Do: Write help only when it changes how a person fills the field. Avoid: Repeat the label as placeholder, description and tooltip. Why: Repeated copy creates noise without adding a constraint or example. Do: Associate each error with the editable control and preserve exact values while repairing it. Avoid: Replace task-specific errors with a generic invalid badge or normalize a machine identifier in help text. # JSON

Inspect a JSON tree with recursive redaction before rendering.

## Choose this component

Choose Json for structured inspection and recursive redaction. Use Code for literal source and Input or Textarea for editing.

## Usage rules

### json-usage

Owner: json.

When a nested object can contain sensitive keys.

Do: Apply the redaction predicate recursively before rendering and copying, and pass only JSON-compatible values.

Avoid: Redact the visible tree while copying the original object or assume collapsed nodes are concealed secrets.

Why: Collapsed presentation is not a data boundary; clipboard content must use the same safe source.

Checked by: review only. Look for: Redact a sensitive key nested in objects and arrays, then copy from a bounded preview. Rendered and copied values use the same recursively safe source.

Source evidence:
- src/components/v4/ui/json.tsx
- src/pages/design-system/examples/json/default.tsx

### json-redaction-before-copy

Owner: json.

When structured inspection includes fields that must not be revealed.

Do: Use named-key or predicate redaction before rendering and copying, and distinguish bounded preview limits from the complete safe copy source.

Avoid: Assume collapsed nodes conceal secrets, copy the unredacted input or describe a truncated preview as the entire document.

Why: Collapsed or limited content can still be present in data; redaction must govern both visible and copied values.

Checked by: review only. Look for: Redact nested values, limit preview depth and copy. The copy contains the full safe document, never the hidden original, and invalid input with redaction requested stays fully redacted.

Source evidence:
- src/components/v4/ui/json.tsx
- src/pages/design-system/examples/json/default.tsx

## State guidance

- collapsed: Keep full safe source available for copy even when preview depth is bounded.
- invalid: Treat unparseable input as literal code, or fully redact it when redaction was requested.

## Presentation rules

Do: Use a bounded tree to expose actual structure.

Avoid: Expand enormous objects by default or decorate each primitive as a badge.

Why: Unbounded structure overwhelms inspection and makes important fields harder to find.

## Import and exports

- src/components/v4/ui/json.tsx
- src/components/v4/ui/json-model.ts
- src/components/v4/ui/code.module.css

Exports: Json, redactJson, prepareJson. Source TypeScript defines the API.

## Behavior

- maxLines follows computed line height and the shared body inset, so text enlargement preserves the requested visible-line bound.
- Objects and arrays expand independently with two levels initially open.
- Named-key or predicate redaction replaces values before rendering and copying.

## Accessibility

- Each node's toggle is a named button that announces whether the node is expanded.
- The tree is a named scroll region.

## Use cases

- Inspect JSON-compatible data with explicit recursive redaction. Preview limits and expansion govern reading, not safe copy completeness.

## Limits

- Only JSON-compatible values are supported. Preview depth and node counts are bounded; Copy retains the full safe source.
- Invalid JSON strings display as literal code; with requested redaction, unparseable input is fully redacted.

# Loader Loaders by level: BootLoader while the app or session boots, RouteProgress while a navigation resolves, and Loader for a page or a region of unknown shape. ## Choose this component Page loader, Skeleton or the table's loading rows: while a whole page or its chunk loads and none of it is on screen, use the page loader. Once the page has rendered, show Skeleton shapes for a card, panel or chart of known shape, and the table's loading rows (DataTable loading with loadingRows) for rows inside a table that is on screen. Use Spinner with a label for inline status and Progress for a known count. ## Usage rules ### loader-label Owner: loader. When a region shows a Loader. Do: Pass a present participle that names the object, such as Loading secrets. Avoid: Use a bare Loading label or no label at all. Why: People need to know what is loading and where it will appear. Checked by: review only. Look for: Read each Loader label and check that it names what loads. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/loader.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/loader/default.tsx ### loader-unknown-shape Owner: loader. When a region is waiting for data. Do: Use Loader only when the shape of the result is unknown. When it is known, show Skeleton shapes like the loaded state and announce the wait with a status. Avoid: Cover known rows, cards or a chart with a blanket Loader. Why: Matching shapes keep the layout still and show what is coming; a centered spinner hides both. Checked by: review only. Look for: For each Loader, check whether the loaded content has a known shape. If it does, replace the Loader with Skeleton shapes at the same size. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/loader.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/loader/default.tsx ### loader-page-level Owner: loader. When a whole page, or the lazy chunk that renders it, is loading and none of it is on screen yet. Do: Render the page loader, Loader size page, as the Suspense fallback or the page body, labeled with the page it loads. Avoid: Show a Spinner, bare Loading text or a blank area, or put the page loader over a table or region inside a page that has already rendered. Why: One page-level treatment tells people the whole page is on its way; inside a rendered page, Skeleton and the table's loading rows keep the layout still. Checked by: review only. Look for: Check each Suspense fallback and page-level loading branch renders Loader size page; the suspense-fallback lint check of rule/page-loading catches single-line fallbacks. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/loader.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/loader/default.tsx ### loader-boot-level Owner: loader. When the app or the session is booting and no shell is on screen: the root route's pending state on /v4, the auth layout, or the organization route that authenticates and loads the session. Do: Render BootLoader with a label that names what boots, such as Loading Infisical, Loading sign in or Loading your organization. Avoid: Wrap a Loader in a V4Scope of your own for boot, label it Loading, or use BootLoader for a page inside the shell, where the page loader sits in the content area. Why: BootLoader themes itself before V4Scope exists and matches the pre-JavaScript ground, so boot goes from the HTML to the shell on one ground with one label. Checked by: review only. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/loader.tsx ## State guidance - loading: The Spinner centers in the region after the delay, with its label under it. - loaded: The children replace the Loader in place. ## Presentation rules Do: Keep the page loader's assembly as the one entrance flourish. Avoid: Restart the page loader every time data refreshes. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Loader composes Spinner with its label, description and delay; it adds the area that centers it and marks the region busy. - With loading false it renders its children and nothing else. - The default delay of 300ms keeps fast loads from flashing. - Loader is for content whose shape is unknown. When the loaded shape is known (rows, cards, a chart), show Skeleton shapes that match the loaded state instead, as the reload in the example does. - Size page is the page loader: it fills a page body while the page or its lazy chunk loads, before any of the page is on screen. - BootLoader is the page loader for app and session boot, before the shell exists: the router's root pending state and a route that authenticates the session or loads the organization. It fills the viewport, or its container with fill container, and themes itself from storage the way the app theme does (a ?theme= or session preview outside live orgs, else the named theme for the scheme the shared light, dark or system preference resolves to), so it needs no V4Scope. It appears only after duration-slow, so instant navigations show nothing, then creeps toward nine tenths of the width; when the navigation resolves it fills and fades out. Reduced motion shows a still full-width bar instead. It reads no router: the app passes pending from its own router state. ## Accessibility - Spinner's label carries one polite status announcement; the region sets aria-busy while loading. - BootLoader announces its label through the same Spinner status. - RouteProgress is aria-hidden: the destination page's title and its own loader announce the change, so the bar adds no second announcement. ## Use cases - Use the page loader (size page) as the Suspense fallback for a page or a lazy page chunk, and for a page whose first data has not arrived, labeled with the page it loads. - Use Loader at base size around a card, panel or sheet of unknown shape while its first data loads, with a label that names the object. - Use BootLoader for the root pending state on /v4 and for routes that boot the session or the organization, before the shell renders. - Mount one RouteProgress in the v4 root for in-app navigations. ## Avoid - Nest a Loader inside a page Loader, or put one inside a button. - Cover a table that is already on screen with a Loader; use its loading rows. ## Limits - For an inline status beside text, use Spinner with a label directly; Loader only fills areas. - Use Progress for a known count and Skeleton for a known layout. # Multi-select Choose several known options without closing after each selection. ## Choose this component Choose MultiSelect for several known values from a searchable list. Use Checkbox for a few visible independent choices and Combobox for one value. ## Usage rules ### multi-select-usage Owner: multi-select. When a selection grants access only after a host operation succeeds. Do: Keep selected option ids as draft state and let the host authorize and persist the result. # Row link A typed route link whose target stretches over its table row or Card, with a disabled fallback. ## Choose this component Choose RowLink when the row is a link to a URL: people can open it in a new tab, copy it and see it in the status bar. Choose DataTable's onRowActivate when activating the row runs an in-page action such as opening a details Sheet. Use one or the other per table. ## Usage rules ### row-link-vs-row-activate Owner: row-link. When a whole DataTable row should respond to a click. Do: Use RowLink in the primary cell when the row navigates, and onRowActivate when it opens something in place. Avoid: Navigate from onRowActivate with router.navigate, or set both on one table. Why: Navigation from a click handler has no href, so new-tab, copy link and middle-click stop working; setting both gives each row two targets and two tab stops. Checked by: review only. Look for: ui:lint row-activate-navigates flags an onRowActivate that navigates, inline or through a function in the same file. Check imported handlers and tables that pass onRowActivate while rendering RowLink by hand. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/row-link.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/row-link/default.tsx ### row-link-sheet-row Owner: row-link. When activating a row opens its record in a Sheet or Dialog on the same page. Do: Render the name as a quiet link Button (variant link, underline hover) that runs the table's onRowActivate handler, so the row draws no chevron. When the sheet is addressable by URL and the name is a RowLink to it, pass chevron={false}. Avoid: Keep RowLink's chevron on a row that never leaves the page, or add a chevron or Open action to the actions tail for the same sheet. Why: The chevron promises a new page; on a row that opens a sheet it sends the person somewhere they never go. Checked by: review only. Look for: Open each sheet-opening table and check that no row shows a chevron and the actions tail has no Open action. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/row-link.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/row-link/default.tsx ### row-link-chevron Owner: row-link. When a table row navigates to another page through RowLink. Do: Keep the default trailing chevron and place RowLink last in its cell's flex line, so the chevron lands on the cell's trailing edge. Avoid: Draw a second chevron or arrow in the row, put badges or hints after the RowLink, or turn the chevron off on a row that goes to another page. Why: The chevron is the row's only visual sign that activating it navigates; content after the link pushes it off the trailing edge. Checked by: src/components/v4/ui/row-link.test.tsx. Renders an enabled, a disabled and a chevron={false} RowLink and checks the aria-hidden chevron is present on the first two and absent on the third. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/row-link.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/row-link/default.tsx ## State guidance - hover: Table rows keep their own hover tint; a Card gets a translucent ink overlay. The chevron turns from muted to ink. - disabled: Muted text, no overlay and no href; give the reason elsewhere in the row. ## Presentation rules Do: Keep row actions as ordinary buttons in the table's actions tail, the sticky last column, outside the link. Avoid: Wrap the whole row in an anchor. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - RowLink takes link, the app's link target, and renders one anchor through CipherLink. The row or Card becomes the positioning context through :has(), so hosts need no linked prop. - Buttons, inputs, checkboxes, comboboxes, switches, other links, tooltip triggers and anything marked data-row-interactive inside that host sit above the overlay and keep their own click. - The link text truncates with an ellipsis; pass title to show the full value on hover. - A trailing chevron-right marks the row as navigation. # Secret input Type or paste a secret value that stays masked until the field is focused. ## Choose this component Choose SecretInput to type or paste a secret value in a form. Use SecretValue to show a value the host already holds with reveal and copy, and SensitiveEditor when the stored value must be fetched only on explicit reveal. ## Usage rules ### secret-input-masked-editing Owner: secret-input. When a form collects a new secret value or edits one the person may view. Do: Pass the real value and onChange; the field masks itself while unfocused and edits the real text when focused. Avoid: Store HIDDEN_SECRET_VALUE in form state or port a v3 SecretInput to SecretValue, which cannot be edited. Why: The mask is display only, so saving it would overwrite the secret with dots, and the old v4 name pointed at a read-only display. Checked by: src/components/v4/ui/migration-traps.test.tsx. Renders a value with a zero-width space, checks the textarea shows the mask and the warning, then focuses it and checks the real value. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/secret-input.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/secret-input/default.tsx ### secret-input-sans-muted-placeholder Owner: secret-input. When a SecretInput sits beside an Input, such as a name and value pair in a quick-add row or a form. Do: Leave the font and placeholder color to the primitive: the body role in the UI sans for the value and placeholder, and the shared muted field placeholder. Avoid: Set a mono font on the value or the placeholder, or override the placeholder color in a page stylesheet. Why: A secret value is typed text, not literal machine output, and Geist Mono's wider, heavier strokes make a muted placeholder read near full ink beside the sans one next to it. Checked by: review only. Look for: Compare the computed ::placeholder color and font family of a SecretInput and an Input in peach and dark; both must match. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/secret-input.module.css - src/pages/design-system/examples/secret-input/default.tsx ## State guidance - masked: Blur always masks a non-empty value; the warning stays visible. - invalid: Pass invalid or let Field mark it, and keep the error message beside the field. ## Presentation rules Do: Explain the invisible characters by type and code point in the warning. Avoid: Strip the characters silently or reveal the value in the tooltip. Why: A pasted no-break space or zero-width space breaks the secret where it is used, and the person decides whether it belongs. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/secret-input.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/secret-input.module.css - src/components/v4/lib/invisible-characters.ts Exports: SecretInput, SecretInputProps, HIDDEN_SECRET_VALUE. While the textarea is not focused and the value is not empty it shows HIDDEN_SECRET_VALUE, the same 16-dot mask as v3; focus binds the real value for editing, selection and copy, and blur masks it again. The mask is never passed to onChange. - It is a textarea, so pasted line breaks are kept. Use Combobox when the list needs search. ## Usage rules ### select-usage Owner: select. When the saved option is temporarily unavailable. Do: Keep its label visible and explain why a different choice may be needed rather than silently clearing it. Avoid: Offer hundreds of unsearchable rows or encode an empty placeholder as a real option. Why: The popup should make one known choice easy to inspect and change. Checked by: review only. Do: Keep the label in the selected trigger and the associated description right-aligned on the menu option's row. Let the trigger fill its field, keep descriptions short and widen the menu with menuWidth when long metadata must stay readable. Avoid: Concatenate the description into the selected label or grow the trigger beyond the preview. Why: Supplementary context must remain readable without changing the saved identity or pushing neighboring controls away. Checked by: review only. Look for: Select the long described option at 320px with doubled root text. The trigger fills its field, contains only the selected label, and reopening shows the label and associated description on one row, truncated with an ellipsis when the menu is narrower than the text. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/select.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/select/metadata.tsx ## State guidance - empty: Show a placeholder until a valid option is selected. - disabled: Explain the prerequisite outside a disabled trigger because it cannot receive focus. - long selected label: Keep only the option label in the trigger. The bounded trigger can truncate a long label; reopening shows the label and associated description in the menu, and menuWidth gives long metadata more room. ## Presentation rules Do: Group options only when the group names help distinguish choices. Avoid: Add icons and separators to every row of a short homogeneous list. Why: Unnecessary grouping slows the simple selection the control is intended to support. Do: Keep low-level trigger sizes and menu placement as separate supported compositions. Avoid: Treat every high-level prop as a low-level Content prop or describe an in-memory Select as searchable. Why: Select supports fewer options than the lower-level parts it wraps, so a prop that works on one may not exist on the other. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/select.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/picker.module.css Exports: Select, SelectContent, SelectGroup, SelectItem, SelectLabel, SelectScrollDownButton, SelectScrollUpButton, SelectSeparator, SelectTrigger, SelectValue. # Sensitive editor Explicit reveal and replacement editing with host-owned access and persistence. ## Choose this component Choose SensitiveEditor when a stored secret should be fetched only after explicit reveal. Use SecretValue only when the host already permits plaintext in memory, and SecretInput to type or paste a new value. ## Usage rules ### sensitive-editor-usage Owner: sensitive-editor. When a person may replace a stored value without permission to reveal it. Do: Keep stored identity separate from an empty replacement draft and let Save await the host callback. Avoid: Fetch or prefill the stored value merely to open replacement mode. Why: Editing a replacement does not require reading the existing secret. Checked by: review only. Look for: Replace without reveal, reject a save, change stored revision and reject clipboard permission. No fetch occurs for replacement, the draft survives failure and old plaintext remasks. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/sensitive-editor.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/sensitive-editor/lifecycle.tsx ### sensitive-editor-sans-muted-placeholder Owner: sensitive-editor. When the editor shows a stored value or opens the replacement box. Do: Keep the value and the replacement text in the UI sans body role, with the placeholder in muted like every field placeholder. Avoid: Render the secret value in mono or dim the placeholder to faint. Why: A secret value is typed text, not literal machine output, and faint is for disabled text only, so a faint placeholder reads as a disabled field. Checked by: review only. Look for: Open Replace without viewing in peach and dark and compare the placeholder's computed color and font with an Input's. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/data.module.css - src/pages/design-system/examples/sensitive-editor/lifecycle.tsx ### sensitive-editor-capability-and-revision Owner: sensitive-editor. When a stored secret can be revealed, replaced or copied under changing permission. Do: Keep stored id and revision current, offer only permitted callbacks and preserve replacement without retrieval; await actual clipboard and save promises. Avoid: Pass stored plaintext just to draw a mask, reveal while starting replacement or promise clipboard expiry or reliable memory erasure. Why: Masking is presentation, while retrieval, persistence and permission are host responsibilities with separate lifecycles. Checked by: review only. Look for: Change revision during reveal, reject replacement and retry, then copy with a rejected writer. Stale plaintext does not reappear, the draft survives failure and success follows actual settlement. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/sensitive-editor.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/sensitive-editor/lifecycle.tsx ## State guidance - revealed: Remask on Escape and on stored identity or value changes; let the host enforce permissions. - save-error: Keep the replacement draft and error until retry or explicit cancellation. ## Presentation rules Do: Distinguish the stored value from a replacement draft. Show pending work and keep rejection beside the retry action. Avoid: Render a fake masked string as the editable value, announce a save before its promise resolves or claim masking is authorization. Why: A mask is presentation; confusing it with actual data can overwrite or expose the wrong value. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/sensitive-editor.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/data.module.css Exports: SensitiveEditor, SecretValue, CopyButton, StoredSecret. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Stored identity and replacement draft are separate. Replacing never fetches the stored value. One-line sensitive hosts use 32px with 24px nested reveal/copy actions; multiline content may grow. - Blocked actions stay visible and disabled, never hidden: without onReveal (no view permission) Reveal and Copy render disabled with a reason, and without onSave or with readOnly, Replace without viewing renders disabled. Copy is gated only by the view permission: while the value is masked, Copy fetches it through onReveal and writes it without revealing it. - Host reveal/save promises receive AbortSignal. Identity/revision change invalidates pending work and clears plaintext. - The stored value display and the replacement box use the body role in the UI sans, and the replacement placeholder is muted, the same token Input's placeholder uses. - Copy awaits the actual write before success notification. Failures preserve current draft and show recovery. CopyButton size sm/md/lg describes a 32/36/40px host and produces a 24/28/32px nested action, defaulting to sm. iconOnly defaults to false; icon-only actions retain their accessible label. ## Accessibility - Every editor has a label and announced loading/result state. - Escape cancels an unsaved edit and masks the value again. The editor keeps whitespace and normal keyboard editing. - Neither the masked display nor its accessible name contains the stored value. ## Use cases - Expose only the permitted reveal, replacement and copy capabilities, with stored identity separate from any replacement draft. ## Limits - Masking does not grant or enforce authorization. Hosts decide permission and perform fetch/decryption/save. - Read-only SecretValue already receives plaintext in memory. Use SensitiveEditor to defer retrieval until explicit reveal. - SecretValue was called SecretInput in earlier v4 builds. v3 SecretInput is an editable field, so it ports to the v4 SecretInput, not to SecretValue. - Plaintext cannot be erased from browser memory reliably; remasking removes rendered/session references only. - Copy writes to the system clipboard.
